Forensic findings CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context: A generic institutional records office maintains document series with unique identifiers, creation dates, and custodian assignments. Each record contains standardized metadata fields (title, version, status, timestamp) and substantive fields defined by the record template. Records flow through defined channels (intake form, review queue, approval log, archive) with role-based access controls. Retention schedules specify lifecycle durations per document type. Auditing relies on immutable audit trails capturing actor ID, action, timestamp, and before/after values. Document chains show revision history, and cross-references link related records. Access logs record who opened, modified, or exported each record.

2) What occurred: The actor created a series of intake forms documenting donor candidates with financial-obligation fields. The actor populated consent documents with signature fields, date fields, and attestation blocks. The actor generated medical evaluation records with eligibility fields and clinician signature fields. The actor prepared referral documents routing recipient information through named clinic entities. The actor maintained correspondence records via email channels discussing scheduling and document transmission. The actor created a registry tracking donor-recipient pairings with status fields updated across multiple dates.

3) Materials/access observed: The actor accessed the donor intake template, the consent form template, the medical evaluation template, the referral form, and the pairing registry. The actor used a named account with administrator-level access to the records system. The actor accessed the email archive of the clinic coordination channel. The actor referenced a set of clinic contact records and a set of financial-obligation documentation templates.

4) Indicators & artifacts: The consent forms show signature fields populated without corresponding verification timestamps. The medical evaluation records contain eligibility fields with values inconsistent with standard clinical terminology. The referral documents list clinic names not present in the standard clinic registry. The pairing registry shows status transitions occurring outside business hours across multiple dates. The email correspondence contains scheduling language referencing document transmission without attachment verification entries. The financial-obligation documentation template was accessed and modified to include additional fields not in the standard template. Audit trail shows a single named account making all modifications across all document types.
